LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a plain Arch Linux `.SRCINFO` metadata file for the `portable` package (Kraftland/portable), a seccomp/bubblewrap-based application sandbox. It contains only declarative `pkgbase`, `pkgdesc`, `pkgver`, `arch`, `license`, dependency, optdepend, and `source` fields — no executable code, no shell snippets, and no obfuscated or encoded content whatsoever.

The single source entry points at the project's own upstream GitHub repository over HTTPS, pinned to `#tag=20.2`, which is the expected and legitimate source for this package. There is no `curl | bash` pattern, no download from an unrelated third-party host, no network exfiltration, no credential or filesystem access, and no build-time logic at all (`prepare()`/`build()`/`package()` live in the PKGBUILD, not here).

Minor hygiene observations only, none of which rise to a security threat: the `source` uses a git *tag* rather than a pinned commit (tags are mutable, and `pkgver` follows the tag name), and an `md5sums` value is declared for that git source even though checksums for VCS sources are effectively unused. Both are ordinary packaging choices and not indicators of malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Clean SRCINFO metadata; upstream-only git source, no code.</summary>
</security_assessment>
